title: Add TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER (16kHz mono SharedAudioBuffer)
description: Add a new global SharedAudioBuffer for transcription in audio_processing/shared_buffer.rs. This buffer holds 16kHz mono audio for the real-time transcription engine. Similar to MIC_BUFFER/SYSTEM_BUFFER but mono and at 16kHz sample rate. Max capacity ~10s at 16kHz = 160k samples. Single channel (mono) since whisper expects mono. Add TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER as lazy_static global.

title: Pipeline step: voice-to-tasks — transcribe, run Claude CLI, create beads issues
description:
End-to-end flow: user records voice notes with task ideas → transcription → pipeline step runs Claude CLI (claude -p) with a prompt that parses the transcript and creates beads issues (bd create) automatically.

**User story:** I ramble into mic about what needs to be done. Pipeline transcribes, sends to Claude with a system prompt like 'Parse this transcript into actionable tasks. For each task, run bd create with appropriate title, description, type, and priority.' Claude creates the issues directly.

**Depends on:**
- nbp-h7h (Pipeline step: run Claude Code / Codex CLI as agent) — the CLI agent connector
- Working transcription pipeline

**Implementation:**
- Create a prompt template that instructs Claude to: (1) parse voice transcript into discrete tasks, (2) for each task run bd create with --title, --description, --type, --priority, (3) output summary of created issues
- Pipeline config: Transcribe step → LLM step (optional: clean up/structure the raw transcript) → CLI agent step (claude -p with the bd-create prompt)
- The CLI agent step needs access to bd CLI in PATH and the .beads/ directory
- Prompt should instruct Claude to: infer priority from context/urgency, pick correct type (bug/task/feature), write descriptions with enough context for another agent to understand, add dependencies if mentioned

**Example flow:**
1. Record: 'ну и ещё надо починить что олама показывается как клауд модель, и ещё фильтровать модели опенаи, там 30 штук нахуй не нужных'
2. Transcription: raw text
3. Claude CLI parses → creates nbp-xxx (fix Ollama classification) + nbp-yyy (filter OpenAI models)

**Considerations:**
- Language: user speaks Russian, tasks should be in English (or configurable)
- Deduplication: prompt should instruct to check bd list first before creating duplicates
- bd CLI must be available in the agent's PATH

title: Show pipeline cards during active recording
description:
During recording, the detail view should show: 1) Recording name (as now), 2) Available pipeline cards to assign while recording is in progress, 3) Already assigned pipelines list. User can pre-assign pipelines during recording so they auto-execute when transcription completes. 

Layout idea: available pipelines as a side panel on the right, not stacked below. This way the recording info stays on the left, pipelines on the right - no scrolling, better use of horizontal space on desktop.

Clean, minimal UI - no clutter. Needs UI/UX Pro Max skill review for layout.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (round 1)

1. Missing required "already assigned pipelines list" during recording.
The task explicitly requires the recording detail view to show both available pipeline cards and the already assigned pipelines list while recording is in progress. The change adds the new pre-assign panel (`src/index.html:130` and `src/main.js:1014`), but the existing assigned-runs UI (`#pipeline-status-section` at `src/index.html:205`) is still hidden because `showDetailView` sets `hideContent` when recording (`src/main.js:1027`) and only renders pipeline status when `!hideContent` (`src/main.js:1032`). Result: during active recording, users can see/toggle cards but cannot see the assigned list required by the task.

2. CSS selector is too broad and regresses Settings layout while a recording is active.
`body.is-recording-active .detail-container` (`src/styles.css:3569`) applies to every `.detail-container` in the app, not just the recording detail view. The Settings view also uses `.detail-container` (`src/index.html:247`), so opening Settings during an active recording will switch the settings container to a horizontal row layout intended for the recording screen. This is a cross-view regression and violates task scope.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (round 2)

1. Required "already assigned pipelines list" is still hidden during active recording.
The assigned list UI is still nested inside `#detail-content-grid` (`src/index.html:141`, `src/index.html:205`). `showDetailView` still computes `hideContent = isRecording || isProcessing` and hides that entire grid during recording (`src/main.js:1027`, `src/main.js:1029`). Calling `renderPipelineStatus(id)` unconditionally (`src/main.js:1032`) does not satisfy the requirement because the parent container remains `display: none`, so the assigned pipelines list is not visible while recording.

2. The assigned-runs list will not refresh when users pre-assign/unassign from the new recording panel.
The new recording-panel card handler only re-renders the card panel and chips after toggling (`src/main.js:840`, `src/main.js:862`, `src/main.js:863`) and never refreshes the runs list (`renderPipelineStatus` / `showDetailView`). The only automatic refresh path is the `pipeline-progress` event listener (`src/main.js:429`, `src/main.js:433`), but backend `assign_pipeline` and `remove_pipeline_run` do not emit `pipeline-progress` events (`src-tauri/src/pipeline_engine.rs:1387`, `src-tauri/src/pipeline_engine.rs:1431`). Result: even after the visibility issue is fixed, the "already assigned" list will stay stale during panel interactions.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (round 3, final)

1. The recording-detail layout still breaks on narrow windows because the new side-panel layout is forced at all widths.
`body.is-recording-active #detail-view .detail-container` switches the detail screen to a row layout unconditionally (`src/styles.css:3569`), while `.recording-pipeline-panel` has a fixed `width: 260px` (`src/styles.css:3581`) and the base `.detail-container` has no wrap/breakpoint fallback (`src/styles.css:1000`). This overflows/compresses the recording detail view on narrow desktop windows and mobile-sized viewports. The task description specifically frames the side panel as a desktop layout idea, so this needs a responsive fallback (stacked layout) instead of forcing the desktop arrangement everywhere.

2. The new "already assigned pipelines" UI is not reliable because recording-time pipeline assignment still has two unsynchronized paths.
The capture section (including the existing `#pipeline-chip-bar`) remains visible during recording (`src/index.html:41`, `src/styles.css:523`). `handleChipClick` mutates only `currentAssignedPipelines` and re-renders chips (`src/main.js:1898`) without backend `assign_pipeline`/`remove_pipeline_run` calls and without refreshing the new recording panel (`src/main.js:1900`, `src/main.js:1909`). The new recording panel, however, uses backend assignment/removal (`src/main.js:840`, `src/main.js:857`, `src/main.js:864`), and the "Your Runs" list is rendered from backend states via `get_all_pipeline_states` (`src/main.js:444`, `src/main.js:450`). Result: while recording, users can toggle assignments from the chip bar and the detail panel/list will drift out of sync (badges/list don’t reflect the actual auto-execute set consistently), so the required "already assigned pipelines list" is not dependable.

title: CLI Agent: add model selection mode (dropdown + advanced command override)
description:
Add configurable model selection for CLI Agent because model choice can require non-trivial flags/arguments.

Proposed UX:
- Default mode: simple model dropdown (curated/common models)
- Advanced mode: command-line override field for custom model invocation/flags

Important example:
- For OpenCode, support provider-model style selection (e.g., provider + model pair), not just a flat model name
- UI should allow mapping to OpenCode-specific arguments/templates

Why:
- Dropdown improves discoverability for common use
- Advanced command mode supports complex/edge model selection patterns
- Provider-model pairing is required for some CLIs (including OpenCode)
acceptance_criteria:
1) User can choose model via dropdown in standard flow
2) User can switch to advanced mode and provide custom CLI model args/command template
3) OpenCode supports provider-model selection (provider + model pair)
4) Validation prevents invalid combinations (e.g., dropdown + conflicting manual args)
5) Clear preview of final command before run
6) Saved pipeline preserves selected mode and values

title: CLI Agent: show supported CLIs with installed/not-installed status; add OpenCode
description:
In CLI Agent configuration, OpenCode is missing and users cannot see what is installed locally.

Required behavior:
- Show supported CLIs list (expected set: 3)
- Include OpenCode in supported CLIs
- Detect local availability per CLI and show status:
  - Installed
  - Not installed

UX expectations:
- User can immediately understand which CLIs are usable
- If selected CLI is not installed, show actionable guidance (install command/path hint)

Acceptance criteria:
1) Supported CLI list includes all 3 targets (including OpenCode)
2) Each CLI displays installed/not-installed status
3) Non-installed CLI cannot run silently; clear error/disabled run state
4) Status refresh works after installation without app restart (or with explicit refresh action)

comments.author: hltm-loop
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL: 1) OpenCode install guidance is incorrect and points to a non-existent package. `src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs:11` and `src/pipeline-builder.js:24` use `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/opencode`, but `npm view @anthropic-ai/opencode` returns E404. This breaks actionable install guidance and causes incorrect installed/not-installed expectations. 2) OpenCode execution command is invalid, so the new CLI path cannot execute successfully. `src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs:121-123` runs `opencode -p <prompt>`, but current OpenCode CLI does not support `-p` (confirmed via `npx --yes opencode-ai --help` and `npx --yes opencode-ai -p "hello"`, which exits with code 1 and usage output). This violates acceptance criterion #3 because selecting OpenCode leads to runtime failure even when installed. 3) The touched validation tests are now broken. `src-tauri/src/pipelines.rs:962` still asserts the old error text (`'claude' or 'codex'`) after validation messages were updated to include OpenCode. `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml test_cli_agent_step_invalid_cli_fails -- --nocapture` fails on this assertion. 4) CLI list rendering has a race that can show an empty supported-CLI dropdown. `src/pipeline-builder.js:623-624` starts `loadCliAvailability()` in the background without awaiting it, while `src/pipeline-builder.js:960-967` renders options from `cliAvailabilityCache || []`. If the step editor opens before the async load completes, no supported CLIs are shown, violating acceptance criteria #1/#2 for initial render.
FIX SUGGESTION: Replace OpenCode install hints with the actual install package (`npm install -g opencode-ai`) in backend constants and frontend fallback data; switch OpenCode invocation to a supported non-interactive command path (for example `opencode run <message>` after verifying exact flags); update CLI-agent validation tests to match the new accepted set/messages and run the touched tests; and make CLI option rendering deterministic by awaiting availability load in `showStepEditor` or rendering a fixed 3-item fallback list until availability refresh completes.

title: Transcribe button resets to clickable state after navigating away and back
description:
Start transcription → navigate away from recording → come back → transcribe button is active again as if nothing is running. Can trigger duplicate transcription.

**Root cause:** Transcription state is only in frontend JS memory. Re-rendering the detail view resets button state. No backend check.

**Fix approach — in-memory lock on backend:**
- transcription.rs — add a Mutex<HashSet<String>> of active recording IDs as managed Tauri state
- Before starting transcription: check set, if already running → return early
- On completion/error: remove from set
- Add command is_transcribing(recording_id) → bool for frontend to query
- Frontend: main.js — when rendering detail view, call is_transcribing() and disable button if true

**Why in-memory, not metadata:** If app crashes mid-transcription, in-memory lock auto-clears on restart. Metadata lock would stay 'running' forever and require manual recovery logic.

title: Deleted pipeline still executes after recording ends
description:
Repro: assign pipeline to recording during active recording → delete the pipeline while still recording → stop recording → deleted pipeline still runs processing.

**Root cause likely:** Pipeline assignment is stored/cached at assign time (recording start or mid-recording). When recording stops and processing kicks off, pipeline_engine reads from the cached assignment list, not checking if the pipeline definition still exists.

**Fix:**
- pipeline_engine.rs — before executing a pipeline, verify it still exists in pipelines store. Skip with a warning if deleted.
- Alternatively: when a pipeline is deleted (pipelines.rs delete_pipeline), also remove it from all pending/assigned pipeline runs that haven't started yet.
- Frontend: if a pipeline was assigned but got deleted before execution, show a 'skipped — pipeline deleted' status instead of running it.

Those runs stay in metadata as waiting because execute_pipeline is never called. 2) src/main.js:520 catches any get_pipeline error and silently skips execution, which masks non-not-found failures (e.g. pipelines.json read/parse errors) and drops assigned pipelines without surfacing the real error. Backend already handles deleted pipelines in execute_pipeline by marking the state Partial (src-tauri/src/pipeline_engine.rs:494).
FIX SUGGESTION: Only skip on explicit not-found responses (inspect error string/code) and let other errors log/fail normally. For waiting runs, either call execute_pipeline and rely on backend deleted-pipeline handling to move state out of waiting, or add a dedicated backend status transition for deleted/skipped pipelines before continue.

title: Research: sandboxing strategy for CLI agent pipeline steps
description: When running Claude Code / Codex as a pipeline step (nbp-h7h), what level of sandboxing is needed? Options: 1) No sandbox - full user permissions (simplest, most capable, least safe), 2) Docker container - isolated, mount only needed files (safer, slower), 3) Limited scope - agent gets transcript only, outputs text, no actions, 4) Permission-based - agent proposes, user approves. Need to decide before implementing nbp-h7h.
notes:
Decision: No sandbox. Rationale: (1) Transcript-only mode loses the core value prop - file/codebase access is why we spawn CLI agents vs using the existing LLM connector. (2) Docker is overkill for a desktop app, requires Docker installed, and codebase access needs bind mounts anyway. (3) Permission-based approval breaks post-recording automation. (4) Pipelines are user-authored config, not external attack surface. Implementation guidance for nbp-h7h: spawn CLI as subprocess with user-configured working_directory as cwd, pass transcript via temp file or stdin, capture stdout as step output, enforce timeout from config. Working directory scoping provides implicit blast radius control without a full sandbox layer.
Skipping: label 'needs-brainstorm' indicates this task needs human input before it can proceed.
close_reason: Decision made: no sandbox, documented in notes

title: Auto-transcribe not triggered after recording despite setting enabled
description:
Transcription is set to auto-run in settings, but after stopping a recording it doesn't start automatically. User has to manually trigger transcription.

**Root cause likely:** audio.rs stop_recording / finalization — after recording completes, the auto-transcribe setting from config is not checked or the transcription call is not fired. Possibly the event chain breaks: recording stops → finalization → should check config.auto_transcribe → call transcribe_recording.

**Fix:**
- audio.rs — after finalization, read auto_transcribe setting from config
- If enabled, trigger transcription automatically (call transcription logic or emit event for frontend to pick up)
- Frontend fallback: main.js — on 'recording_complete' event, check setting and call transcribe if enabled

title: Implement realtime_transcription module (local Whisper sliding window)
description: Create src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs with the local Whisper real-time transcription engine. Architecture: sliding window (5s window, 1s step). Uses whisper-rs state.full() called repeatedly on the transcription buffer. Context between chunks via prompt_tokens. VAD integration (simple energy-based initially, Silero later). Emits Tauri events 'realtime_transcript_delta' with { text, is_final } payload. The engine reads from TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER, processes chunks, and emits incremental transcript updates. Must handle: start/stop lifecycle, thread management, Whisper model loading (reuse existing whisper model infrastructure from transcription.rs).
notes: Code merged to dev. Review issues remain: (1) VAD computed over full 5s window delays finalization, (2) duplicate Whisper model loading (should reuse transcription.rs), (3) Drop doesn't join worker thread. All need fixing.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL

Reviewed `dev...HEAD` (base branch is `dev` in this repo; no `main` branch exists) and the task commit `f9ebba0` for `nbp-r6s`.

Findings:

1. Correctness: VAD is computed over the entire 5s sliding window, which delays finalization and keeps the engine "speaking" long after speech stops.
   - `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:498` uses `compute_rms(&window)`.
   - `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:552` only emits the final transcript when that VAD result flips false.
   - Because `window` intentionally retains up to 5 seconds of prior audio (`src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:492-496`), old speech energy remains in the RMS calculation for several steps. In practice this can delay `is_final=true` emission (and `prompt_tokens` reset) by up to ~5 seconds after the user stops talking, and keeps running Whisper on mostly-silent windows.

2. Completeness / task requirement mismatch: the task explicitly requires reusing existing Whisper model-loading infrastructure from `transcription.rs`, but the new local transcriber duplicates that setup inline instead of sharing it.
   - New duplicate load path: `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:453-461`
   - Existing Whisper setup path: `src-tauri/src/transcription.rs:708-727`
   - This creates two independent Whisper initialization/config code paths that can drift.

3. Lifecycle / thread management: `LocalTranscriber::Drop` does not join the worker thread, it only flips the stop flag and drops the `JoinHandle`.
   - `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:439-443`
   - If a caller drops/restarts a transcriber without calling `stop()` first, the old worker can continue consuming `TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER` and emitting events until it next checks the flag / finishes inference, causing overlap with the new worker.

title: Implement MCP connector: HTTP transport, UI config, backend execution
description: MCP connector stub exists (ConnectorType::Mcp in pipelines.rs, engine arm returns not-yet-implemented). Need to: (1) add connectors/mcp.rs with MCP Streamable HTTP transport (JSON-RPC initialize + notifications/initialized + tools/call per 2024-11-05 spec), (2) implement MCP execution in pipeline_engine.rs, (3) add MCP validation in pipelines.rs (url and tool fields required), (4) fix MCP config editor in pipeline-builder.js (change data-field from 'server' to 'url' with proper URL placeholder), (5) add MCP preset to PROCESSING_PRESETS, (6) add 'mcp' to needsConfig. Implementation for mcp.rs is already drafted as untracked file at src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs — review and include.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (round 1)

Findings:

1. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:160` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:161` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:182`
The MCP connector only parses `tools/call` responses as a raw JSON body and silently converts parse failures to `Null`. For Streamable HTTP, compliant servers may return `text/event-stream`; in that case the SSE payload will not parse as JSON, and this code will still write a successful `status: done` output with empty content instead of handling the streamed JSON-RPC message/result.

2. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:79` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:110` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:129`
The implementation never reads the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the `initialize` response and never sends it on `notifications/initialized` or `tools/call`. Streamable HTTP session handling requires reusing that session header on subsequent requests when the server provides it, so this will fail against stateful MCP servers.

3. `src-tauri/src/pipelines.rs:293`
MCP validation checks that `tool` exists and is a string, but it does not reject an empty string. `{"tool":""}` passes validation even though the task requires `tool` to be a required field, and execution then sends an empty tool name.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (round 2)

Findings:

1. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:182` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:184` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:226`
The SSE handling still treats the `tools/call` response as a single JSON-RPC message by grabbing the first `data:` line in the whole stream. Streamable HTTP responses can include multiple SSE messages (e.g. notifications/progress before the final JSON-RPC response). If the first event is a notification, this code parses that object, finds no top-level `error`, then writes a successful `status: done` output with empty content. It needs to parse SSE event boundaries and select the actual `tools/call` response message (matching the request id) instead of the first `data:` line.

2. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:208` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:226` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:259`
The connector only treats top-level JSON-RPC `error` as failure. MCP tool execution failures are returned as a successful JSON-RPC response with `result.isError = true`; this implementation ignores `result.isError`, extracts the text, and writes `status: done`. That misreports failed tool calls as successful pipeline steps.

3. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:79` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:88` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:103`
`initialize` is sent, but its JSON-RPC response body is never parsed. A server can return HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC `error` (for example protocol/version rejection); this code treats that as successful initialization and continues to `notifications/initialized` and `tools/call`. The initialize response must be parsed and validated before proceeding.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (round 3, final)

Findings:

1. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:205` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:206` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:214` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:216`
The `text/event-stream` parser is still line-based, not SSE-event-based. It only matches lines starting with `"data: "` (with a space), so valid SSE payload lines formatted as `data:{...}` or `data:{...}` without the optional space are ignored. It also does not assemble multi-line `data:` fields into a single event payload. Both are valid SSE encodings, so compliant MCP servers can return a correct `tools/call` response that this code fails to parse and then reports as `"no response matching request id"`.

2. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:110` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:112` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs:129`
`initialize` response validation still fails open. The code only inspects `error` if the body parses as JSON, and treats parse failures (or any JSON object without an `error` field) as successful initialization. That means HTTP 200 responses with malformed/non-JSON bodies or invalid JSON-RPC shapes will incorrectly proceed to `notifications/initialized` and `tools/call` instead of failing initialization.

title: Model download has no cancel action
description:
Model download UX lacks a cancel/stop control. User cannot abort an in-progress download.

Observed:
- During model pull/download there is no Cancel button/action
- If wrong model selected or bandwidth needed elsewhere, user is stuck

Expected:
- Clear cancel action available while download is in progress
- Cancellation is immediate and safe

Acceptance criteria:
1) Show Cancel button for active downloads
2) Cancel stops backend download task and network stream
3) UI state switches to cancelled (not failed) with clear message
4) Partial artifacts are cleaned up or marked resumable consistently
5) User can re-start download afterward without app restart

comments.author: hltm-loop
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL: 1) Cancellation is not immediate and does not reliably abort an in-flight transfer. File refs: src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:154, src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:158, src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:172-179. `cancel_llm_download` only flips an atomic flag, but `download_llm_model` blocks in `send().await` and then `stream.next().await` before checking that flag. If the connection stalls or no chunk arrives, cancel does not stop promptly (request timeout is 3600s), so requirement #2 (immediate cancel + stop backend/network work) is not fully met.
2) Cancel button state is not restored after a cancelled normal download, so subsequent active downloads can lose a working cancel action. File refs: src/integrations-settings.js:608-609 and src/integrations-settings.js:592-600. On cancel click, button becomes disabled with "Cancelling..."; in the catch path for `.llm-download-btn`, code hides progress and re-shows Download but never resets `.llm-cancel-download-btn` or rerenders the card. A retry can show a disabled cancel button, violating requirement #1 across retries.
FIX SUGGESTION: For #1, implement abortable download flow (per-download cancellation token/channel + `tokio::select!`) so cancellation interrupts both request startup and body streaming immediately. For #2, in the `.llm-download-btn` catch path either reset `.llm-cancel-download-btn` state explicitly or rerender (`renderLocalLlmModels`) before the next attempt.

title: Real-time transcription should write directly into transcript; no provider picker
description:
Clarification for real-time transcription behavior:
- Real-time is not required as a separate on-screen live text mode
- It should continuously feed/write into the recording transcript pipeline so final transcript appears with minimal delay
- Slight delay is acceptable; reliability is the priority
- User should NOT choose a separate real-time provider in UI
- Do NOT implement real-time on cloud models; real-time path should be local-only

Rationale:
- Cloud real-time adds complexity/cost/latency with low value for this workflow
- Goal is dependable transcript readiness, not flashy live rendering

Expected direction:
- One transcription flow that writes to transcript reliably during/after recording
- Provider selection is unified/simplified (no separate realtime provider control)
- Local engine handles realtime-ish chunking; cloud remains non-realtime fallback/manual path if needed
acceptance_criteria:
1) During recording, local transcription chunks append to the same transcript storage/output path
2) On stop, transcript is already mostly ready; no separate live-text dependency required
3) No separate realtime-provider selector in settings for this feature
4) Realtime path does not use cloud models/APIs
5) Flow is reliable even if slightly slower than live rendering
6) Existing transcript UX remains a single source of truth

This removes the already-written realtime transcript instead of using it as the primary path. 3) Requirement #1 not met for in-progress persistence: during active speech the code only updates `last_text` in memory (`src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:156-160`) and writes `transcript.json` only on speech->silence or final stop (`src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:161-175`, `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:193-201`). FIX SUGGESTION: Rebase/cherry-pick `nbp-3ev` onto a clean branch so diff contains only realtime-transcription files and `nbp-3ev` tracker metadata. Keep one transcript flow by avoiding automatic post-stop `transcribe_recording` overwrite when realtime writing is enabled (or merge/continue from realtime output instead of deleting it). Persist realtime transcript incrementally while speech is active (append/write at step intervals, not only at silence boundaries). In `local_llm` cancellation select branch, ignore non-matching model IDs and continue waiting so cancellation remains per-model.

title: Tap mixed audio into TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER in realtime_mixer
description: In audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs, after mixing mic+system but before OGG encoding, downsample the mixed signal from 48kHz stereo to 16kHz mono and push into TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER. Use rubato (already in project) for high-quality downsampling. Mono = average of L+R channels. This feeds the real-time transcription engine with clean mixed audio.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL

1. `src-tauri/src/audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs:250` and `src-tauri/src/audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs:283` encode silence to the OGG stream but do not feed the same frames into `TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER`.

   The task asks to tap the mixed audio before OGG encoding. Right now only the non-silence mix path (`feed_transcription_resampler(...)` at `:230`) is tapped. When the mixer inserts catch-up silence or final wall-clock padding, the transcription stream skips those frames entirely, so `TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER` diverges from the encoded stream/timeline and can compress gaps between speech segments.

2. `src-tauri/src/audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs:274` and `src-tauri/src/audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs:377` do not fully flush the `rubato` resampler tail.

   `flush_transcription_resampler` only pads and processes one final input chunk with `resampler.process(...)`, and it does nothing when `accum` is empty. `rubato::Resampler` keeps delayed output frames for sinc filters; those remaining frames must be drained at end-of-stream (via the partial-processing flush path, including the exact-multiple-of-chunk case). As written, the transcription buffer loses the final delayed samples and can truncate the end of the stream.

2. The transcription resampler tail is now flushed with `process_partial(...)` for leftover buffered input and `process_partial(None)` to drain delayed sinc output (including the exact-multiple-of-chunk case).

Rationale:

- Remove step-name input field from step edit UI

Acceptance criteria (if approved):
1) No editable step-name field in step editor
2) Step names render as stable auto-generated labels
3) Existing pipelines with custom names are handled gracefully (preserve display or migrate)
4) No breakage in references/export/import where step name is used

title: Real-time transcription during recording
description:
Real-time transcription during recording — transcript ready when recording stops.

## Подход

**Локальный (Whisper):** sliding window — 1s шаг, 5s окно. whisper-rs state.full() вызывается многократно. Контекст между чанками через prompt_tokens. VAD через Silero модель чтобы не гонять инференс на тишине.

**Облачный (OpenAI Realtime API):** WebSocket на wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?intent=transcription. Модели: gpt-4o-mini-transcribe (дешевле), gpt-4o-transcribe (точнее). Аудио: PCM16 24kHz mono. VAD server-side.

**Google STT:** только gRPC, нет нормального Rust SDK для стриминга — не рекомендуется. Deepgram как альтернатива (WebSocket, 300ms latency, есть Rust SDK).

## Архитектура

```
MIC/SYSTEM BUFFER (48kHz stereo)
    → Downsampler (rubato, уже есть в проекте)
    → TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER (16kHz mono для Whisper / 24kHz для OpenAI)
    → TranscriptionEngine:
        Local: whisper-rs state.full() sliding window + Silero VAD
        Cloud: WebSocket → OpenAI Realtime API
    → Tauri events ('realtime_transcript_delta', { text, is_final })
    → Frontend: живой текст транскрипта во время записи
```

## Модели и ресурсы (Apple Silicon)

| Модель | RAM | 5s аудио на M1 | Рекомендация |
|--------|-----|-----------------|--------------|
| Tiny | ~390MB | ~0.15s | Минимальная точность |
| Base | ~500MB | ~0.3s | Оптимальный баланс |
| Small | ~1GB | ~0.75s | Лучше точность |
| Medium+ | 2.5GB+ | >1s | Не подходит для real-time |

Рекомендация: **Base** или **Small** с Metal. На 8GB маке всё влезает.

## Что делать

1. **audio_processing/mod.rs** — добавить TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER (SharedAudioBuffer, 16kHz mono)
2. **audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs** — тапнуть микс в transcription buffer после смешивания, до OGG кодирования
3. **Новый модуль: realtime_transcription.rs** — движок: sliding window для local, WebSocket для cloud
4. **transcription.rs** — команды start/stop real-time transcription
5. **Cargo.toml** — tokio-tungstenite для WebSocket (cloud путь)
6. **main.js** — слушать realtime_transcript_delta, показывать текст live во время записи

## Конфиг

Настройка в settings: вкл/выкл real-time transcription, выбор модели (local base/small), fallback на post-recording если машина слабая.

title: Ollama: 'Failed to load models' error in settings
description:
Ollama provider shows 'Failed to load models' in UI. Model list cannot be loaded.

Observed:
- In LLM settings/provider section for Ollama, fetch fails with generic error
- User cannot select/use local Ollama models

Expected:
- App successfully loads models from configured Ollama host
- If unreachable/misconfigured, error message is actionable (host, port, timeout, service status)

Investigation targets:
1) Ollama endpoint resolution (base URL, protocol, port, trailing slash handling)
2) Network/connectivity + timeout handling
3) Error mapping from backend to frontend (avoid generic failure text)
4) Retry behavior and cached fallback handling

Acceptance criteria:
- Models load when Ollama is reachable
- Clear actionable error when not reachable
- Manual test covers valid host, wrong host, Ollama stopped, and recovery

title: Check local model freshness - detect outdated versions
description: For locally downloaded models (Ollama), detect if a newer version is available upstream. Ollama uses manifest digests (SHA256) to track versions - compare local digest against remote. Show 'Update available' badge on outdated models. Refresh button to check all at once.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text: REVIEW FAIL: 1) Existing downloaded models are skipped if they were downloaded before this feature because freshness checks only read the .sha256 sidecar and do not hash existing files (`src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:281`, `src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:328`). The UI then treats an empty result map as success and shows "All models are up to date" (`src/integrations-settings.js:313`, `src/integrations-settings.js:315`), which is a false positive and does not meet the task requirement for local downloaded models. 2) The update/re-download path does not clear cached freshness state before re-render (`src/integrations-settings.js:273`), so a previously stale `llmFreshnessData[modelId]` value can keep showing the "UPDATE AVAILABLE" badge after a successful update (`src/integrations-settings.js:178`). Delete flow does clear it (`src/integrations-settings.js:294`). 3) `sha2` was added as a direct Rust dependency (`src-tauri/Cargo.toml:53`), but `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` was not updated; the `nbp` package dependency list still omits `sha2` (`src-tauri/Cargo.lock:2705`).

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text: REVIEW FAIL: 1)  reads the entire model file into memory with  () before hashing. These registered models are 2.4-4.9 GB (, , , ), so freshness checks for pre-existing downloads can allocate multi-GB RAM and fail/OOM instead of reliably checking local models. Hash the file in a streaming manner (buffered reader + incremental ) and then write the sidecar. 2)  intentionally omits models when remote checks fail (, ), but the UI still shows  whenever  (, ) without confirming that every downloaded model was checked. A partial/total network failure becomes a false success. Return explicit unknown/error status (or checked/failed counts) and only show the success toast when all downloaded models were actually checked and none are outdated.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL: 1) `compute_and_cache_sha256` reads the entire model file into memory with `std::fs::read` (`src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:290`) before hashing. These registered models are 2.4-4.9 GB (`src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:40`, `src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:49`, `src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:58`, `src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:67`), so freshness checks for pre-existing downloads can allocate multi-GB RAM and fail/OOM instead of reliably checking local models. Hash the file in a streaming manner (buffered reader + incremental `Sha256`) and then write the sidecar.

2) `check_all_llm_freshness` intentionally omits models when remote checks fail (`src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:327`, `src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:349`), but the UI still shows `All models are up to date` whenever `updateCount === 0` (`src/integrations-settings.js:314`, `src/integrations-settings.js:316`) without confirming that every downloaded model was checked. A partial/total network failure becomes a false success. Return explicit unknown/error status (or checked/failed counts) and only show the success toast when all downloaded models were actually checked and none are outdated.

title: Model download progress UI breaks card layout; redesign progress bar
description:
Model download progress currently renders inside the model block/card in a way that breaks layout.

Observed:
- Progress element distorts/breaks the surrounding block
- Visual quality is poor during active downloads

Expected:
- Stable card layout during download
- Clean progress bar component, optionally with percentage text

Acceptance criteria:
1) Progress UI does not resize/break parent card layout
2) Dedicated progress bar style with proper spacing and overflow handling
3) Percentage is shown (or clearly omitted by design) and updates smoothly
4) Works for 0%, in-progress, complete, and error states
5) Responsive behavior verified on narrow widths

Implementation notes:
- Constrain progress container dimensions
- Avoid text wrapping/overflow that changes card height unpredictably
- Add regression check for multiple concurrent downloads

comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL: 1) Scope violation: this task is for the model download progress UI, but the branch diff includes unrelated tracker and backend freshness changes: `.beads/issues.jsonl:7`, `.beads/issues.jsonl:14`, `.beads/issues.jsonl:104`, `src-tauri/src/config.rs:69`, `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:263`, and `src-tauri/src/local_llm.rs:909-1034`.

FIX SUGGESTION: Rebase/cherry-pick nbp-87b onto a clean branch with only progress-bar files. Keep freshness/cache backend work in its own issue branch. If freshness type changes are kept, add explicit migration/deserializer for legacy boolean cache entries before changing the field type. Update cached UI mapping to read `CachedFreshnessInfo` fields (`update_available`, `error`, etc.). In download/update error handlers, keep the progress row visible, add `.error`, and render failure text instead of hiding the component.

Need to decide before implementing nbp-h7h.","notes":"Decision: No sandbox. Rationale: (1) Transcript-only mode loses the core value prop - file/codebase access is why we spawn CLI agents vs using the existing LLM connector. (4) Pipelines are user-authored config, not external attack surface. Implementation guidance for nbp-h7h: spawn CLI as subprocess with user-configured working_directory as cwd, pass transcript via temp file or stdin, capture stdout as step output, enforce timeout from config. Need to decide before implementing nbp-h7h.","notes":"Decision: No sandbox. Rationale: (1) Transcript-only mode loses the core value prop - file/codebase access is why we spawn CLI agents vs using the existing LLM connector. (4) Pipelines are user-authored config, not external attack surface. Implementation guidance for nbp-h7h: spawn CLI as subprocess with user-configured working_directory as cwd, pass transcript via temp file or stdin, capture stdout as step output, enforce timeout from config. title: Implement cloud real-time transcription (OpenAI Realtime API WebSocket)
description: Add cloud transcription path to realtime_transcription module. WebSocket connection to wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?intent=transcription. Models: gpt-4o-mini-transcribe (cheaper), gpt-4o-transcribe (more accurate). Audio format: PCM16 24kHz mono. Server-side VAD. Protocol: send input_audio_buffer.append events with base64-encoded audio chunks, receive conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta and .completed events. Requires tokio-tungstenite. Resample from 16kHz to 24kHz for OpenAI (or tap at 24kHz directly).
notes: 3 review fails, partially fixed. Remaining issues: (1) WebSocket close frame swallowed without error event, (2) needs final review pass. Type annotation fix merged to dev. Do NOT pick up until review issues resolved.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL

1. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:118` sends a malformed `transcription_session.update` payload.
   The code wraps configuration fields under a `session` object, but the Realtime transcription protocol expects `input_audio_format`, `input_audio_transcription`, and `turn_detection` at the top level of the `transcription_session.update` event. With the current shape, the server will reject or ignore the config, so the session is not configured as requested.

2. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:261`, `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:275`, and `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:288` swallow runtime WebSocket failures and return success.
   On send/read errors the loop logs and `break`s, then the function returns `Ok(())`. That bypasses the error propagation path in `CloudTranscriber::start()` and no `realtime_transcription_error` event is emitted for mid-session failures. The transcription session can stop silently on network/protocol errors.

3. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:200`, `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:233`, and `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:288` drop buffered audio on shutdown.
   Audio is only sent when `resample_accum.len() >= 1024`, but there is no shutdown flush (`process_partial`) before returning. Any remaining <1024 input samples (plus resampler delay) are lost, which truncates the tail of the last utterance.

4. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:95` and `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:98` abort the task immediately in `stop()`, which prevents the graceful close path at `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:288` from running during normal stop.
   This makes the stop flag ineffective and increases the chance of losing final buffered audio / closing the socket abruptly.

Notes:
- Could not run `cargo check` in this environment because `cargo` is not installed (`/bin/bash: cargo: command not found`).
- Protocol shape check verified against the OpenAI Speech-to-Text Realtime guide example for `transcription_session.update`.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL

1. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:207` and `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:213` still drop queued shutdown audio from `TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER`.
   The loop exits as soon as `should_stop` is set, before it drains the shared transcription buffer. The new shutdown flush only processes `resample_accum` (`src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:290`), so any samples already queued in `TRANSCRIPTION_BUFFER` at stop time are never popped/resampled/sent. This still truncates the tail on normal stop.

2. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:292` does not fully flush the rubato resampler delay line.
   `process_partial(Some(&[remaining]), None)` handles the partial input chunk, but the code never follows it with a `process_partial(None, None)` drain call. rubato keeps delayed frames internally for sinc filtering, so the final delayed samples are still lost at shutdown.

Notes:
- Could not run `cargo check` in this environment because `cargo` is not installed (`/bin/bash: cargo: command not found`).

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL (final round)

1. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:319` does not compile.
   `resampler.process_partial(None, None)` leaves the generic input type (`V`) unconstrained, so Rust cannot infer the type for the `None` argument. This needs an explicit type annotation (same pattern already used in `src-tauri/src/audio_processing/realtime_mixer.rs:411` with `None::<&[Vec<f32>]>`).

2. `src-tauri/src/realtime_transcription.rs:271` still swallows server-initiated WebSocket closes and returns success.
   The `Message::Close(_)` branch just `break`s without setting `loop_error`. That means an unexpected server close (including protocol/auth failures surfaced as a close frame) exits `run_cloud_transcription()` with `Ok(())`, so `CloudTranscriber::start()` does not emit `realtime_transcription_error` for that runtime failure path.

Notes:

title: Fix settings layout — all new/updated sections wider than original ones
description:
All new/updated settings sections (Models, Integrations) are wider than original ones (Audio, Theme).

**Root cause:** Original settings use .detail-container (max-width: 900px) and .settings-input-group (max-width: 400px). New sections use custom containers that don't inherit these constraints.

**Fix:** Use ui-ux-pro-max skill. Audit all settings sections in styles.css, ensure consistent max-width. New sections (Models grid, Integrations panels) must respect same container constraints.

title: Pipeline step: run Claude Code / Codex CLI as agent
description: Add a pipeline step type that spawns Claude Code or Codex CLI with the transcript + custom prompt as input. Unlike a simple LLM API call, this gives full agent capabilities: file access, code generation, tool use, multi-step reasoning. Use cases: auto-create beads tasks from meeting notes, generate code from discussion, run complex analysis that needs codebase context. Config: select CLI (claude/codex), prompt template, working directory, timeout. Output: agent's final response + any side effects (commits, tasks created).
notes: Implemented CLI agent connector. New files: connectors/cli_agent.rs (subprocess spawn with timeout, stdin piping, tilde expansion). ConnectorType::CliAgent added with serde rename 'cli_agent'. Tokio process+time features added. UI: CLI Agent preset in PROCESSING_PRESETS, config fields (cli select, prompt textarea, working dir, timeout), connector select option, auto-open on add. Numeric input fields now saved as numbers in config.

comments.author: Sergey Kopanev
comments.text:
REVIEW FAIL: 
1) Missing tracked source files for the new connector modules. `src-tauri/src/connectors/mod.rs:1` and `src-tauri/src/pipeline_engine.rs:991`/`:1002` now reference `cli_agent` and `mcp`, but `git status --short` still shows `?? src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs` and `?? src-tauri/src/connectors/mcp.rs`. If this patch is landed as the current diff, the backend will not compile because the module files are not included. Track the required files (or remove the references).
2) Timeout is not actually enforced for the CLI agent subprocess. In `src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs:129`, `tokio::time::timeout(...)` wraps `child.wait_with_output()`, but the timeout branch returns an error without killing/reaping the spawned `claude`/`codex` process. A timed-out agent keeps running in the background. Kill the child and wait for it before returning the timeout error.
3) MCP regression plus scope creep in a CLI-agent task. The UI editor still writes `server` for MCP (`src/pipeline-builder.js:857`), while the new preset/backend validation expect `url` (`src/pipeline-builder.js:159`, `src-tauri/src/pipelines.rs:280`). Editing/saving an MCP step produces config that fails validation/runtime. Either fix the MCP field mismatch in this change or remove the unrelated MCP changes from `nbp-h7h`.

comments.author: hltm-loop
comments.text:
BLOCKED after 3 failures: review still fails on correctness + scope.

Findings:
1) `src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs:210` invokes Codex as `codex --quiet`. Current Codex CLI rejects this flag (`unexpected argument --quiet`) and non-interactive mode is `codex exec`, so `cli_agent` steps configured with `codex` fail immediately instead of running the agent.
2) `src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs:106` / `src-tauri/src/connectors/cli_agent.rs:124` timeout handling still returns after dropping `wait_with_output()` and only relies on `kill_on_drop`; it does not explicitly kill + wait/reap the subprocess before returning the timeout error, so the prior timeout-cleanup review issue remains unresolved.
3) Scope violation: branch diff includes unrelated tracker database data (`.beads/issues.jsonl:1` new file, 72 lines) in a CLI-agent connector task.

Validation: `bun run check` passes (warnings only).`
